result.summary: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with [[noreturn]]. It also suppresses Clang's -Wc++23-lambda-attributes warning on annotated lambdas and migrates bare C exit and abort calls (abort(), exit(), _Exit()) to their std:: counterparts in <cstdlib>.
result.problem: Functions that never return (such as unconditional throwers, exit handlers, and fatal assert stubs) lack [[noreturn]] annotations, which can lead to compiler analysis false positives such as spurious missing-return warnings. Without an enforced compiler warning flag, newly added non-returning functions easily omit the attribute.
evidence: PR description: "Missing [[noreturn]] attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556."
Commit 934c041f07 adds -Wmissing-noreturn to warning flags to enforce the attribute systematically.
result.scope_notes: Touches bundled third-party or extracted libraries (src/ipc/libmultiprocess commit marked [nomerge], and src/util/subprocess.h), which the author has submitted upstream.
result.changed_since_previous: Expanded the standard library refactor commit to replace bare abort() and _Exit() calls across validation, sync, and txdb with std::abort() and std::_Exit(), alongside the previous std::exit() replacements.
result.card: Enables the -Wmissing-noreturn compiler warning flag in CMake and annotates non-returning functions, methods, and lambdas across the codebase with [[noreturn]]. It also migrates bare C runtime abort and exit calls to std::abort, std::exit, and std::_Exit, while suppressing Clang -Wc++23-lambda-attributes warnings on annotated lambdas. This prevents compiler analysis false positives, such as spurious missing-return warnings, where the compiler cannot tell that a branch unconditionally terminates.

risk.why: Mistakes are limited to compile-time attribute and warning flag changes or minor std:: namespace qualification on abort/exit calls.
